summary: The finite set of React Native names the Frontier HUD imports, with one decision per name. Every name is `supported` with the subset below; a prop or member outside the subset fails visibly or is ignored in a documented way, on mount and on update.

decisions.supported: the name exists and behaves as the subset says
decisions.explicit-error: the name or member throws where it is used
decisions.documented-ignore: the name or member is accepted and changes nothing, for a stated reason

audit.note: A dated snapshot (docs/PARITY.md, docs/compatibility/README.md); nothing validates it and this manifest does not edit it. Each entry below carries the audit's row as recorded and says whether it is stale.

names.name: View

audit.name: View
audit.note: The accessibility props the host maps (label, hint, role, state, live region, hidden, onAccessibilityTap) reach Godot's AccessKit tree (GF-20, first slice); the rest of RN's accessibility props and the OS settings are open.

names.runtime: RN's original View.js over the base view config of the platform (src/base-view-config.js); the facade checks the declared props and the style names

subset.style: the names of controlViewConfig.validAttributes.style; another name throws `Godot View does not implement style <name>`
subset.ref: ViewInstance, the public instance with the pointer-capture methods

names.name: Text

audit.name: Text
audit.note: Runs RN's original Text.js. onTextLayout (outer paragraph only) and the Yoga baseline come from the host's measureLines; the outer paragraph presses through RN's Pressability. fontStyle italic (a synthetic slant: the bundled fonts have no italic face) and textDecorationLine, textDecorationColor and a solid textDecorationStyle are painted by the host; oblique and the double, dotted, dashed and wavy lines fail. Span press, selection, adjustsFontSizeToFit, font scaling, head/middle ellipsis, inline views and Text accessibility remain open; the default size stays 18, not RN's 14.

names.runtime: RN's original Text.js over the paragraph of the host (src/text.jsx)

subset.style: the text styles of src/base-view-config.js (textStyleAttributes) and the View styles; fontStyle is normal or italic, textDecorationLine none, underline, line-through or both, textDecorationStyle solid
subset.nested: a nested Text is a span: it takes no press or responder prop and no numberOfLines

names.name: Pressable

audit.name: Pressable
audit.note: Carries the mapped accessibility props (aria-* converted as RN's Pressable does, accessible by default, disabled as the disabled state); focus, keyboard and custom actions are open.

names.runtime: Pressability's press props around the View of the host's Control (src/components.jsx); the keys RN does not declare are dropped before the Control

subset.style: an object, or a function of { pressed }
subset.children: nodes, or a function of { pressed }
subset.hover: onHoverIn and onHoverOut are refused: the 0.5 leaves public hover out

names.name: ScrollView
names.runtime: RN's original ScrollView.js behind the public wrapper (src/scroll-view.jsx) over the host's scroll adapter (native/scroll_adapter.cpp); src/prop-scope.mjs decides every prop RN declares for it, and src/scroll-view-contract.mjs checks the values of the ones the host honors and takes the lists' own props off

subset.refused: bounce, paging, snapping, insets, zoom, sticky headers, keyboard handling and pull to refresh: the request that asks for nothing (bounces false, pagingEnabled false, an empty stickyHeaderIndices...) passes and any other fails with `Godot ScrollView does not implement <prop>`; onRefresh and refreshing, which the lists hand to the ScrollView, follow the same rule
subset.ref: scrollTo, scrollToEnd and flashScrollIndicators run on the host; scrollResponderZoomTo and scrollResponderScrollNativeHandleToKeyboard are not declared (the host has no zoom and no keyboard)

names.name: SafeAreaView
names.reason: the HUD's insets: its bars and panels stay inside the notch and the home indicator that the OS leaves out of the window

audit.name: SafeAreaView
audit.note: Retain the pinned upstream compatibility/deprecation behavior; deprecation is not a coverage exemption.

auditStale.current: the audit records a missing public export; SafeAreaView has been exported since the Modal slice, and since V05-08 it is RN's own iOS component with the padding of the window's unsafe bands (docs/PARITY.md)

names.runtime: RN's own RCTSafeAreaViewNativeComponent and SafeAreaViewComponentDescriptor (the component Platform.select picks on iOS) over the host's View control; the host fills the State with the padding that the window's unsafe bands leave of the view's frame (native/display_insets.h), as RCTSafeAreaViewComponentView does, and RN's descriptor applies it to Yoga

subset.props: ViewProps, judged by the table of the View (checkProps("View")); like RN's iOS SafeAreaView it does not go through View.js, so the aria-*, id and tabIndex mappings of that file do not apply and the view config drops those names
subset.style: the names of controlViewConfig.validAttributes.style, as the View's; another name throws `Godot View does not implement style <name>`
subset.insets: iOS and Android report the window's unsafe bands through DisplayServer.get_display_safe_area (screen pixels, converted to Fabric points); every other display server reports none, so the view pads nothing on a desktop. macOS's usable rectangle is never read
subset.padding: UIKit's safeAreaInsets: for each edge the part of the band that the view's frame in the window reaches, rounded to a pixel; the State changes only when a side moved by one pixel plus 0.01 (RCTSafeAreaViewComponentView._updateStateIfNecessary)
subset.ref: ViewInstance, the public instance of the host View

names.name: StyleSheet
names.runtime: the platform's own object (RN's StyleSheet.compose underneath)

limits: create returns the object it is given (no numeric style ids)
setStyleAttributePreprocessor, absoluteFillObject and the other members of RN's module are not part of the subset

subset.select: godot, native and default keys only: the ios and android keys are not selected

names.name: Dimensions
names.runtime: RN's original Dimensions state, fed by the host's metrics; the platform tracks the subscriptions it hands out

subset.get: window and screen: width, height, scale and fontScale (fontScale is always 1)
subset.addEventListener: the change event, which carries { window, screen }
limits: set is RN's native-only entry point and is out of scope

names.name: useWindowDimensions
names.runtime: a store hook over the window metrics RN's Dimensions holds

subset.returns: width, height, scale and fontScale of the window (fontScale is always 1)

notInTheManifest.FlatList: the HUD's lists are short ScrollViews

outOfScope: TextInput, Keyboard, KeyboardAvoidingView and the IME: typed text and the virtual keyboard are out of the 0.5 (ROADMAP.md, `Out of the 0.5`)
public hover and right-click on Pressable (onHoverIn and onHoverOut are refused)
Button, Switch, TouchableOpacity and the other touchables, which keep their own contracts (src/control-contracts.mjs)
rule: A name in neither `names` nor `outOfScope` is not used by the HUD: adding one needs a change to this manifest.

classes.supported: the prop has behavior on this host: the view config lets it reach the host, or the facade or RN's own JS consumes it
classes.ignored: the prop is accepted and changes nothing, with a reason and a source (RN's iOS drops it, or an earlier documented decision)
classes.refused: iOS has behavior that Godot does not implement: the facade throws `Godot <Component> does not implement <prop>` when the value is not null or undefined; `when` narrows the values that fail

propPolicy.undeclaredKeys: A key that React Native does not declare for the component is never checked: RN's Fabric view config drops every name it does not list. The Pressable renders the host's Control, which lists names that only the Control has, so it drops the undeclared keys itself. The props of the earlier Text wrapper (text, fontSize) are the one documented exception and fail with a hint.
propPolicy.source: docs/compatibility/contracts-0.87.1.json (the owner rows of each component's props type, flattened by the TypeScript checker)

Text.fontSize: it is not a prop of RN's Text, set it in style
